builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Sparse PCA with Overlapping Supports: NP-Hardness and an FPTAS
summary: This algorithmic technique replaces heuristic or exponential-time methods for multi-component Sparse PCA with overlapping supports and exact orthogonality constraints. It requires solving a reduced sparse orthogonal Procrustes problem via approximate dynamic programming and algebraic number representation, with runtime exponential in the fixed rank and number of components. It can fail to be practical when the rank or component count grows, as the complexity depends exponentially on these parameters, and it does not address approximate orthogonality or large-scale covariance matrices.
rationale: This is a theoretical algorithm for a specific constrained optimization problem in statistics, not a method for improving inference or training efficiency of AI/ML models on constrained infrastructure.
technique: FPTAS for Sparse PCA with Overlapping Supports

claims.statement: This algorithmic technique replaces heuristic or exponential-time methods for multi-component Sparse PCA with overlapping supports and exact orthogonality constraints. It requires solving a reduced sparse orthogonal Procrustes problem via approximate dynamic programming and algebraic number representation, with runtime exponential in the fixed rank and number of components. It can fail to be practical when the rank or component count grows, as the complexity depends exponentially on these parameters, and it does not address approximate orthogonality or large-scale covariance matrices.
For fixed rank and dimension, the algorithm runs in time linear in $n$ (up to polylogarithmic factors) and provides a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) with exact orthonormality.
